stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Tags confirm its relevance within the transformer, llama, and safetensors ecosystems.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model benefits from Ollama's MLX engine, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
stories.author: Mia Sato
bullet_points: Shopify is expanding its 'agentic commerce' capabilities by allowing AI agents to browse and purchase products.
This update grants more AI agents access to Shopify's catalog, which contains over a billion listings.
The feature allows shoppers to configure their AI agents to handle product purchasing on their behalf.

stories.title: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Epic Games is reportedly shifting its game development paradigm toward an 'AI first' model.
This pivot suggests a move away from traditional, hand-written coding and reliance on AI-free assets.
The change is linked to the development of a delayed Marvel/Star Wars shooter title.

stories.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
stories.author: Christian Schroeder de Witt
bullet_points: New research demonstrates that AI models can be engineered to provably hide arbitrary capabilities.
The study introduces backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights.
These hidden circuits remain difficult to elicit or interpret, challenging current methods of AI safety and capability evaluation.

stories.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
stories.author: Pang Wei Koh
bullet_points: Introduces Prompteina, a novel all-atom protein structure generation model.
The model enables specifying complex design objectives using natural language, similar to text-to-image AI.
Addresses the limitation of existing protein design models requiring dedicated, property-specific inputs.

stories.title: Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts
stories.author: thm
bullet_points: Ledger has confirmed the existence of a hidden chip within crypto wallets.
The chip is allegedly being used by thieves to facilitate cryptocurrency thefts.
The news points to a significant security vulnerability in hardware wallet technology.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating its integration into the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the broader transformer and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.
The updated engine also leads to higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: The feds are looking into reports of Tesla’s robotaxis speeding through school zones
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: NHTSA is investigating reports that Tesla's robotaxis are exceeding speed limits in active school zones.
The scrutiny extends to competitors, with Waymo also facing inquiries regarding safety violations near schools.
The incident highlights growing regulatory oversight and safety concerns surrounding autonomous driving technology.

stories.title: Google wants to host your personal vibe-coded apps in the Play Store
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is planning to facilitate the transition of personal, AI-generated applications into publicly available apps on the Play Store.
This initiative aims to bridge the gap between highly personalized, niche AI tools and mainstream distribution.
The move signals a potential shift in how personalized AI experiences are commercialized and scaled by major platforms.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Argon begins rolling out in Gemini app and Antigravity, but only if you pay
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Gemini 4 Argon is beginning its rollout across the Gemini app and Antigravity.
Access to Gemini 4 Argon features is currently gated behind a paid subscription.
Developers are offered a 50% discount on API rates until November.

stories.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework designed to achieve Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).
Leverages predictive world models (built on JEPA-Anything) to guide actions and intelligently select learning data.
Addresses the limitations of RSI by using observed feedback for policy improvement and conditional world-model adaptation.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the deployment of AI agents using its cloud models.
The integration allows these AI agents to run safely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent environments.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It strengthens Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon users.

stories.title: OpenAI employee arrested for allegedly planting a bug in a conference room
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: An OpenAI engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested for allegedly planting a sophisticated recording device in an office.
The incident involves the discovery of a hidden surveillance device within the company's premises.
Alfozan faces charges related to using a device to intercept oral communications.

stories.title: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Xbox is reportedly adopting AI to manage the complexity of game ports.
The retro gaming scene is experiencing rapid innovation through decompilation and code merging.
Examples of this trend include mods integrating disparate game mechanics (e.g., skateboarding in Call of Duty).

stories.title: Rivian partner Mind Robotics hires Doug Field as president
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe's startup, Mind Robotics, has appointed Doug Field as its new president.
Doug Field previously served as a VP at Apple, where he was involved with the autonomous vehicle project, Project Titan.
The hiring is seen as a significant move for Mind Robotics, which is tied to Rivian's secretive robotics initiatives.

stories.title: Apple’s first smart display is the 7-inch HomeView for $299
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Apple has released its first smart display, named the 7-inch HomeView.
The device is priced at $299.
A key feature is its ability to recognize up to six different users via its camera.

stories.title: They war-gamed dimming the Sun. It went even worse than you think.
stories.author: Karl Mathiesen, WIRED.com
bullet_points: The article discusses solar geoengineering simulations, a high-level climate technology concept.
The focus is on the geopolitical risks and potential negative outcomes of deploying such technologies.
It highlights the intersection of advanced climate modeling and international political strategy.

stories.title: After a 10-year redemption arc, No Man's Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: No Man's Sky is finally being ported to iOS devices (iPhone and iPad).
The game is available for users with iPhone 11 or later models.
This represents a significant platform expansion for the long-running title.

stories.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
stories.author: James Bishop
bullet_points: The research tests the capability of Language Models (LLMs) to perform complex information retrieval from massive, unindexable document collections.
The 'Wikipedia Game' serves as an analogy to evaluate models' ability to navigate knowledge graphs using only article links.
The study compares sentence embedding models against LLMs across multiple Wikipedia languages and academic datasets.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of interpreting black-box vision models using concept-based attribution.
Proposes 'Hide and Seek' (HnS) to overcome limitations of existing methods, such as requiring model weights or large annotated datasets.
HnS aims to provide image-level attribution for concept-level interpretation, a capability lacking in current methods.

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the functional roles of shared components (attention heads) within large language models (LLMs).
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing parallels to task-dependent interactions in biological brain regions.
The study uses graph facts to compare fixed model components across different tasks and measures the impact of interventions on attention.

stories.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
stories.author: Song Liao
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in AI agent development: current tool retrieval methods ignore tool availability during execution.
Introduces RATED, a new framework that merges semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation for tool selection.
Uses a dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for robust semantic matching, enhancing agent reliability.

stories.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
stories.author: Ninareh Mehrabi
bullet_points: The paper addresses the risk of unintended or harmful outcomes when personal AI agents interact across multiple web services.
It proposes 'X-AgentRed' to systematically explore diverse cross-service paths to proactively identify compositional failures.
This method improves upon existing red-teaming techniques that rely solely on prompting LLMs with task descriptions.

stories.title: SpatialASM: Internalizing Active Mentalization for Spatial Reasoning
stories.author: Dahua Lin
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding 'Active Spatial Mentalization' (ASM).
ASM is defined as the human ability to proactively revisit scenes from task-relevant viewpoints to mentally reconstruct spatial layouts.
The paper introduces 'SpatialASM,' a new scalable framework designed to instill this intrinsic visual intelligence into LVLMs.

stories.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
stories.author: Linfeng Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces MC-EvoBench, a controlled Minecraft benchmark designed to audit self-improvement in embodied AI agents.
Addresses the critical challenge of distinguishing true capability acquisition from mere memory retention or resource carry-over in recursive self-improvement.
Focuses on rigorous evaluation methods to separate genuine skill transfer from artifacts like unequal exposure or early execution failures.

stories.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
stories.author: Dharmashankar Subramanian
bullet_points: The research investigates run-to-run variance in semantic query processing when using LLMs.
The study found that even at temperature 0, a significant percentage (0.07% to 10.2%) of row operator outputs change between executions.
The analysis involved re-executing major benchmarks (SemBench, LRO-Bench, UDA-Bench) across 1.2 million model calls.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a new method for concept-level attribution in ML models.
Addresses the limitation of existing concept-based methods, which are often restricted to classification/regression or require extensive data/weights.
Specifically targets the challenge of providing image-level attribution for black-box vision models.

stories.title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
stories.author: Daniel Szelogowski
bullet_points: Introduces DyssomniaNN, a multi-scale biophysical computational framework for modeling human sleep disorders.
Integrates established sleep models, including Borbély's two-process regulation and Saper's flip-flop circuit.
Aims to address the clinical discrepancy between objective sleep duration and subjective daytime impairment in conditions like paradoxical insomnia.

stories.title: Prediction Is Not a Sufficient Memory State
stories.author: Robert Jenkinson Alvarez
bullet_points: The paper distinguishes between a memory that reproduces current predictions and one capable of future learning.
It characterizes this distinction for exact cumulative learning and attention mechanisms.
It establishes a mathematical condition: a continuous recurrent state of fixed dimension exists if and only if the loss function is polynomial.

stories.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
stories.author: Chen Shani
bullet_points: The paper addresses the uncertainty regarding whether Vision-Language Models (VLMs) accurately encode structured spatial relations needed for image reasoning.
It introduces EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), a new metric to test concept consistency under controlled interventions.
A new benchmark, CASP-VL, is proposed to causally test the spatial understanding capabilities of VLMs.

stories.title: Structural Automata for Neural Semantic Parsing
stories.author: Xiao Zhang
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in neural semantic parsing where local token generation doesn't guarantee overall structural validity.
It proposes using structural automata to enforce well-formedness during decoding, post hoc processing, and training stages of DRS parsing.
The work also evaluates the application of these automata to Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) parsing.

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the functional roles of shared components (attention heads) within large language models (LLMs).
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing parallels to task-dependent interactions in the brain.
The study uses graph facts to compare fixed model components across different tasks and measures the impact of interventions on attention.

stories.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
stories.author: Berlin Chen
bullet_points: Introduces OpenPA, a new framework for Automatic Pronunciation Assessment (APA).
Significantly improves practicality by eliminating the need for forced alignment in APA pipelines.
Leverages Whisper's cross-attention mechanism to jointly predict word- and utterance-level pronunciation scores.

stories.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
stories.author: Edgar Chavez-Urbiola
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical problem of language models knowing when to abstain from answering.
Two methods are compared: training the LLM itself versus using a separate, dedicated answer selector component.
The study demonstrates that a learned answer selector improves overall utility on factual question answering tasks using Qwen3-14B.

stories.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
stories.author: Muhammad Shafique
bullet_points: Introduces QTestBench, a new test framework specifically designed to evaluate LLM-generated quantum code.
Highlights the difficulty of testing quantum code due to its probabilistic nature and reliance on numerical tolerances.
Addresses a gap in current quantum benchmarks, which only check for a correct solution rather than robust testing.

stories.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
stories.author: Prayag Tiwari
bullet_points: The paper addresses the problem of 'hallucination' in Large Language Models (LLMs) when used for query expansion.
Current filtering methods treat hallucinations as undifferentiated noise, lacking a mechanistic understanding of term generation.
The proposed solution introduces Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection to trace and tame these hallucinated terms.

stories.title: Error Rate is Not Enough: Costs of Augmentation in Low-Resource ASR
stories.author: David Chiang
bullet_points: The paper investigates the limitations of using only aggregate error rates to evaluate data augmentation in low-resource Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR).
It compares two types of augmentation—audio modification (speed perturbation, SpecAugment) versus text modification followed by synthesis—across multiple languages and data sizes.
The research analyzes errors at the phoneme level, providing a more granular understanding of when and how augmentation methods provide benefit.

stories.title: OpenAI engineer arrested in bugging of executive conference room
stories.author: forthwall
bullet_points: An OpenAI engineer has been arrested in connection with bugging an executive conference room.
The incident raises significant concerns regarding internal security and corporate espionage within major AI labs.
The news highlights ongoing risks associated with insider threats in high-stakes technology environments.

stories.title: PostEra (YC W20) Is Hiring AI Researchers for Drug Discovery
stories.author: morraa
bullet_points: PostEra, a YC-backed startup, is actively recruiting AI researchers.
The focus of the hiring is specifically for applications in drug discovery.
This indicates a growing trend of applying advanced AI/ML to complex biomedical challenges.

stories.title: 11 year old unsoundness bugs found in Rust borrow checker
stories.author: formerly_proven
bullet_points: Security vulnerabilities were discovered in the Rust borrow checker, a core component of the Rust programming language.
The bugs were classified as 'unsoundness' issues, meaning they could potentially undermine the language's safety guarantees.
The discovery is significant for the Rust ecosystem, as the borrow checker is central to Rust's memory safety features.

stories.title: Your AI agent said it blocked the attack. I read the source of 5 tools that check if it's lying.
stories.author: rudratosh
bullet_points: The article discusses a critical vulnerability in AI agents where they might falsely report security actions.
It focuses on the need for advanced testing methods beyond standard test suites to verify AI agent reliability.
The author reviews five tools designed to audit and check the veracity of AI agent claims.
